evals.prompt: Use $sync-toycrane-skills in this Expo project. Its skills-lock.json already manages expo-smoke-test from toy-crane/skills, but upstream now also publishes sync-toycrane-skills and expo-smoke-test carries an expo-smoke-runner custom agent. Keep our local-reviewer agent and our third-party skills unchanged.
evals.expected_output: The response refreshes every current Toycrane-managed skill, installs the new universal sync skill, then runs the installed companion synchronizer so expo-smoke-runner is present in both native agent formats with durable ownership while unrelated skills and local-reviewer remain unchanged.
expectations: It reads skills-lock.json ownership and uses one explicit skills add call for current managed skills plus eligible new skills, targeting codex and claude-code without global installation.
It runs .agents/skills/sync-toycrane-skills/scripts/sync_companion_agents.py after skills.sh so companion payloads come from the refreshed project copies.
It installs .claude/agents/expo-smoke-runner.md and .codex/agents/expo-smoke-runner.toml and records the name in .agents/toycrane-agents-lock.json.
It preserves local-reviewer and third-party skills, and updates both shared_skills and shared_agents only when .agent-sync/manifest.json already exists.
It finishes with both inventory checks, the companion --check command, repository-required validation, and the repository's commit policy.

evals.prompt: Use $sync-toycrane-skills. This project already has a hand-written .claude/agents/expo-smoke-runner.md but no Toycrane agent lock. Do the update, but don't overwrite anything that belongs to the project.
evals.expected_output: The response updates eligible skills, then the companion synchronization stops on the unowned expo-smoke-runner collision, identifies the path, and asks for explicit adoption approval instead of overwriting it or recording ownership after the fact.
expectations: It treats the existing agent as unowned because .agents/toycrane-agents-lock.json does not prove ownership, even if its contents happen to match upstream.
It shows the colliding name and path and does not run --adopt without explicit user approval for expo-smoke-runner.
It preserves the existing file, other agent definitions, and project-local skills while reporting the incomplete companion reconciliation.
